judged_text: The webhook's update branch replaces `credential.key` wholesale with caller-supplied decrypted JSON (`data: { key: keys }`), with no validation against the app's credential schema and no merge with the existing key. A payload containing only the access token and expiry — the exact shape the sync flow documents — wipes the stored refresh_token and other schema-required fields, permanently bricking a working credential with no backup; the `findFirst` at lines 62-70 has no orderBy or type filter, so when a user has multiple credentials for the same app an arbitrary row is overwritten.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the update path does `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })` where `keys` is caller-supplied decrypted JSON (`JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`). There is no schema validation and no merge with the existing stored key, so any omitted fields (e.g., `refresh_token` or other required properties for that app’s credential shape) will be dropped, potentially breaking existing credentials. Additionally, the existing credential is selected via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` with no `orderBy` and no additional discriminator (e.g., type), so if multiple credential rows exist for the same `userId`+`appId`, an arbitrary one may be overwritten.
